dependencies.registry: Authors' original task/language registry: exact kernel bytes, signatures, launches, reference modules, pinned operation tables, and exported proofs. Independent programs at equal shapes cannot replace these inputs.
dependencies.harness: Original proof-agent harness and prompts, segmentation/scaffolding, tool protocol, retries, stopping rules, context compaction, model settings and usage accounting.
dependencies.runs: Original request/response and checker traces, model revisions and original hosted-model outcomes. Offline/free inference does not recover historical paid or closed-model runs.
dependencies.mutants: All 42 original mutant source files, baseline bindings, rule assignments, final-run traces and rejection-channel decisions, including independent second opinions.
dependencies.production: The ten exact adapted production sources, upstream commits, ordered rewrites/departures, argument signatures and launch metadata; nine accepted full-kernel proof projects and the rejected kernel trace.
dependencies.hardware: Original optimized kernels and numerical contracts, complete fastest-vendor baselines, H100 execution for PTX/CUDA and same-device MI300X HIP measurements. MI350X measurements cannot fill H100 cells.
dependencies.semantics: Broader packed/vector readers, arbitrary sparse subgroups and the authors' optimized instruction registry remain software work. Independent complete native activation, weighted RMSNorm, seeded in-place fused RMSNorm, online attention and the llm.c HIP softmax adaptation have scoped actual-launch/trace proofs. Logical-16/32 groups inside physical wave64, one MFMA shape and exact-real wave reduction are supported within their stated profiles. Native softmax uses separate development source-bound checkers and currently issues zero registered frontend source certificates. These profiles do not establish coverage of the original optimized registry. IEEE and rounding error theorems are outside the paper's formal claims, not missing paper results.
dependencies.history: Authors' source tree and development records. An independent implementation cannot recreate historical person-days, original source-line totals or original code-sharing percentages.
dependencies.gqa_export: Authors' supplementary standalone GQA proof project and its pinned toolchain/dependencies; it was not present in the inspected manuscript archive or bounded release endpoints.
dependencies.specification: Authors' elaborated Lean module formalizations, metaprogram/reference tests, accepted shape/precision contracts and associated trusted-assumption reports.

tab:instr-cats.title: Operation schemas
tab:instr-cats.available_evidence: Restricted scalar/memory/control/barrier definitions, full-wave shuffle, one native MFMA shape, and an exact-real six-stage XOR reduction with whole-launch proofs. These do not cover the full original instruction table. A complete native RMSNorm launch now composes aligned logical-16 shuffles inside physical wave64 with both block barriers; this does not cover arbitrary sparse masks or the whole original instruction table. The independent native attention proof composes all nine block phases and four key tiles, shared/private memory and source-ordered nonlinear loops. This is a fixed native profile, not the original instruction census. Seeded mutable buffers, logical32 reductions inside wave64 and complete fused RMSNorm launches are now proved. Native softmax adds three full passes, initialized original-race reachability and repaired complete-grid proofs under its fixed source interpreter.

tab:lib-kernels.title: Ten production kernels: nine certificates and one race
tab:lib-kernels.available_evidence: Four independent upstream-derived accepted families are checked: native multiwave SiLU-and-mul (eight HIP/CUDA certificates); weighted width16384 RMSNorm (four canonical-real exports); seeded in-place fused add RMSNorm (four canonical-real exports, both output buffers); and native N128/D256 online attention (four canonical-real exports). Each retains its own geometry, source departures, standalone replays and paired AMD numerical checks. The independent llm.c HIP softmax study binds both complete sources, proves actual original conflicting accesses from initialization and a racy complete one-row launch, and proves repaired whole-grid race freedom/source-order outputs for rows1..42730 plus canonical-real dense softmax. Its source/replay each check 134 modules, 1530 axiom audits and 11 false controls; all eight CI jobs pass. It issues zero registered softmax frontend certificates. The ten original adapted sources, nine original certificates, historical dialogues and original hardware cells remain unavailable; these independent adaptations do not replace them.

tab:trust.title: Acceptance basis and trust boundary
tab:trust.available_evidence: Fixed source/reference statements, actual launch/RF theorems, standard-axiom audits, isolated rechecks and a pinned exact-real interpretation are implemented. Floating-point cancellation probes demonstrate the limit of interpreting real equality as IEEE equivalence. The independent native RMSNorm exports bind all 70 proof modules, closed source/reference/task statements and optional dependency pins; installed-wheel and standalone rebuild checks pass. Hardware correspondence and IEEE error bounds remain outside the proof. The native online-attention packets freshly rebuild 84 scalar modules and 91 modules with canonical-real semantics, audit 174 and 17 results, and reject 29 and four scoped false claims. Independent archive replays repeat these checks. Canonical-real casts are identities only in that interpretation; IEEE equivalence and floating-point error bounds are unproved. Fused RMSNorm supplies four closed canonical-real source/reference/task exports and standalone replay. Softmax source and replay each check 1530 declarations and reject 11 false claims; 48 rehashed guards protect the original-race scope. All eight CI jobs pass, with 160 ordinary tests passed and nine optional skips. IEEE/error theorems are outside the paper formal claims.

narrative.title: Signature-derived premises, extraction and non-vacuity
narrative.available_evidence: Actual native scalar launches include partial final waves, and one full wave64 reduction has complete execution/RF proofs under its fixed disjoint-buffer interface. Original in-place, stride, packed/vector and general signature coverage is incomplete. The native RMSNorm proof quantifies over all inputs/outside memory and all 1<=rows<256 at the fixed native shape; host alignment and disjointness remain explicit assumptions. The native attention theorem quantifies over all scalar operations, inputs and initial outside memory for every allowed group count 1..65535; the canonical-real specialization additionally proves dense SDPA equality and positive denominators. Disjoint-buffer/profile assumptions remain explicit. A complete seeded-inout fused RMSNorm theorem covers all rows1..255 and extracts both buffers. Repaired native softmax covers all rows1..42730, arbitrary inputs/outside memory and unchanged fuel. These fixed interfaces do not imply arbitrary signatures.

narrative.title: Named refusal boundary and exact-operation idealizations
narrative.available_evidence: Restricted profiles refuse more forms than the paper. Real sum equality is proved for one closed program; finite cancellation disagreements explicitly prevent a floating-point-equivalence claim. Broader operations and original refusal outcomes remain unverified. Complete aligned logical-16 cohorts within physical wave64 and a complete native RMSNorm reduction are now supported. Arbitrary sparse masks and other optimized kernels remain unsupported. IEEE/error theorems are outside the paper formal scope. The fixed native attention development profile now has a complete four-key-tile/nine-phase proof and canonical-real exports. Ordinary-reader bounds and memory restrictions remain; packed/vector, arbitrary sparse subgroups and generalized optimized-kernel support remain software work. The independent fused in-place and native softmax profiles now have complete source execution proofs; repaired softmax also has canonical-real correctness. Native softmax remains a development checker with zero registered source certificates. IEEE/error theorems are outside the paper formal claims.

narrative.title: Race-freedom obligations and scheduling assumption
narrative.available_evidence: Per-program obligations are Lean checked; the scheduling reduction remains a declared trusted passage, not a proved hardware scheduler theorem. The complete native RMSNorm proof classifies every actual input, shared partial/scale and output access through both block epochs and derives race freedom. The native attention proof also derives race freedom from the complete actual runLaunch trace across all nine phases and all blocks, rather than assuming trace classification or a successful finite preflight. Hardware scheduler correspondence remains outside this proof. Fused RMSNorm proves race freedom of its full seeded-inout trace. Softmax proves both original Access members in the actual initialized complete block trace, their conflict, and a supported complete racy one-row launch; repaired whole-grid traces are race-free. Generic original multirow completion is not asserted. No equality to synthetic whole-State snippets or hardware scheduler theorem is asserted.

scope: Every table and outer figure in the submitted preprint input graph, plus explicit non-tabulated result/method anchors. Source enumeration is mechanical; interpretation, evidence mapping and dependency assessments are authored. Rows overlap and are not a completion-percentage denominator. This audit executes no Lean, models or GPUs. It freezes selected published evidence at commit 7437374, including complete independent native weighted/fused RMSNorm and online-attention studies, repaired whole-grid canonical-real softmax, and an actual initialized original one-row race counterexample. No original experimental result is relabeled reproduced. Floating-point behavior is checked numerically within the paper's idealized arithmetic scope.
